newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - April 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - April 18.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories Friday:

* The U.S. trade gap narrowed in February to $10.4 billion from $12.7 billion, with a rise in imports and exports. The government first reported February trade deficit at $11.6 billion but later said it was overstated due to an incorrect oil import figure.
* Microsoft posted an 80 percent earnings increase and a 45 percent revenue gain, which it said was mostly due to Office 97 sales. Results soundly beat expectations.
* Archer Daniels Midland chief executive Dwayne Andreas retired and was replaced by his nephew G. Allen Andreas Jr. Dwayne Andreas would remain chairman.
* Bell Atlantic reported better-than-forecast earnings, citing high demand for second telephone lines.
* Ford and Mazda Motor Corp said they agreed to cooperate on developing some designs, engines and transmissions.
* Digital Equipment posted a 59 percent decline in third quarter profits but still beat expectations.
* Sears, Roebuck stock fell although it reported a 21 percent earnings gain, topping expectations.
* Schering-Plough reported a 14.9 percent increase in profits.
* Industry experts say a slew of promotions by Bell Atlantic Nynex Mobile and AT&T Wireless are a sign a wireless telephone war is starting.
